branch_sync.rename.behind.one: {upstream} has {count} commit that {branch} doesn't have. Pull it first, or deleting {upstream} would lose it.
branch_sync.rename.behind.other: {upstream} has {count} commits that {branch} doesn't have. Pull them first, or deleting {upstream} would lose them.
branch_sync.rename.default: {branch} is the default branch of {remote}, so it is renamed only here: others build on it.
branch_sync.rename.delete_failed: Renamed {old} to {new} and pushed it to {remote} as its upstream, but deleting {upstream} failed: {why}. The old name is still on {remote}.
branch_sync.rename.development: Git Flow uses {branch} as its development branch, so it is renamed only here.
branch_sync.rename.gone: {upstream} is no longer on the remote, so there is nothing to rename there.
branch_sync.rename.local_note: Its upstream setting moves with it; {upstream} is not renamed.
branch_sync.rename.no_upstream: {branch} has no upstream on a remote to rename.
branch_sync.rename.production: Git Flow uses {branch} as its production branch, so it is renamed only here.
branch_sync.rename.push_failed: Renamed {old} to {new} here, but pushing it to {remote} failed: {why}. {upstream} is kept, and {new} still tracks it.
branch_sync.rename.remote_note: Pushes the new name to {remote} and makes it the upstream, then deletes {upstream}. Anyone else using {upstream} has to switch to the new name.
branch_sync.rename.taken: {other} already exists, so the new name can't be pushed there.
